newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Cylinder traded with BP options.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Cylinder traded with BP options.

text.p: British Petroleum was an active stock option on Tuesday as traders took positions before and after the company announced its annual results, dealers said.

Ahead of the results, one large deal was a cylinder strategy from the purchase of 800,000 BP shares at 709p and 1,000 July 700 puts at 33p -- to protect the shares if the stock price falls -- and the sale of 1,000 July 750 calls at 24p.
The net position was delta-neutral so that small changes in the stock price will be offset by changes in the value of the options.
BP announced a 30 percent rise in 1996 replacement cost profit which was roughly in-line with analysts expectations. It expected dividend and earnings per share growth to slow in the current year.
By 1540 GMT, BP shares had fallen 27p to 694p.
Over in mobile phone company Vodafone the main deal was a short strangle from selling 750 July 280 puts at 17p and 750 July 300 calls at 18p.
Maximum profit of 35p will be made at expiry if the underlying shares stay between 280p-300p. Vodafone shares shed 4-1/2p to 283p.

In tobacco-to-insurance group BAT Industries the biggest deal was from a trader who bought 750 April 460 puts at 8p and sold 750 April 550 calls at 11p. Dealers believed the deal may have been to protect a shareholding in BAT.
Also busy was British Airways where a calendar spread was established against selling shares at 595p.
The spread consisted of selling 500 April 600 calls at 21p and buying 500 October 600 calls at 44p.
British Airways shares were 8-1/2p lower at 589p.
